headline.title: In the Weights is your new AI-centric vanity search
headline.summary: The article introduces "In the Weights," a new AI-driven platform that allows users to assess their fitness and health metrics through a personalized scoring system. This tool aims to provide insights into individual performance and wellness, catering to those interested in tracking their fitness journey.

articles.title: [Linkpost] How Transparent Is DiffusionGemma (and why it matters)
articles.summary: A recent transparency audit of the DiffusionGemma text diffusion model, conducted by the GDM interpretability and text diffusion teams, revealed that it is not significantly less transparent than its predecessor, Gemma. Both models demonstrated similar performance in terms of monitorability and interpretability.

articles.title: The Atlantic created a searchable database of the music used to train AI
articles.summary: The Atlantic has launched a searchable database containing four datasets of music used for training AI models, including two large sets with 12 million and 9 million tracks. This initiative, led by reporter Alex Reisner, aims to provide public access to significant training data for AI development.

articles.title: Nobel laureate John Jumper is leaving DeepMind for rival Anthropic
articles.summary: Nobel laureate John Jumper is departing from DeepMind to join rival AI company Anthropic. His exit follows a trend of notable departures from Google DeepMind.

articles.title: Siri AI Hands On: A Smart, Helpful Assistant
articles.summary: The latest iteration of Siri AI features enhanced conversational abilities and improved functionality, making it a more effective digital assistant. Users report that it is now more helpful and responsive in various tasks.

articles.title: From PGP to Mythos: a brief history of export controls that didn’t stop anyone
articles.summary: The article discusses the ineffectiveness of export controls on cybersecurity-related software over the past 30 years, highlighting that previous attempts have failed to prevent the dissemination of such technologies. It questions the likelihood of success for current measures, particularly concerning Anthropic's cybersecurity model, Mythos.

articles.title: Measuring Curriculum Alignment across Topical Coverage, Competency, and Cognitive Depth: A Longitudinal Framework Applied to CS2013 and CS2023
articles.summary: A new study presents a human-in-the-loop pipeline for measuring curriculum alignment in undergraduate computer science programs against international guidelines, focusing on topical coverage, competency, and cognitive depth. This framework is applied longitudinally to assess changes between the CS2013 and CS2023 curricular guidelines.

articles.title: AI4SE and SE4AI Exploration: A Decade Looking Back and Forward
articles.summary: The article reviews the evolution of artificial intelligence in systems engineering over the past decade, categorizing developments into three phases: foundational, applied, and LLM inflection. It highlights the growth of a research community, sparked by a popular 2020 INCOSE INSIGHT special issue, which now attracts over 250 participants to its annual workshop.

articles.title: BrainG3N: A Dual-Purpose Tokenizer for Controllable 3D Brain MRI Generation
articles.summary: Researchers have introduced BrainG3N, a dual-purpose tokenizer designed to enhance the generation of controllable 3D brain MRI images for clinical applications. This approach aims to balance the retention of critical clinical information while facilitating the use of generative models in neurology and neuro-oncology.

articles.title: TelcoAgent: A Scalable 5G Multi-KPM Forecasting With 3GPP-Grounded Explainability
articles.summary: TelcoAgent is a new framework designed for scalable and explainable forecasting of Key Performance Measurements (KPMs) in 5G and next-generation telecom networks. It addresses the limitations of existing machine learning approaches, enhancing their applicability in real-world network management.

articles.title: Rethinking Shrinkage Bias in LLM FP4 Pretraining: Geometric Origin, Systemic Impact, and UFP4 Recipe
articles.summary: The article discusses the limitations of current FP4 training methods for large language models (LLMs), specifically focusing on the Shrinkage Bias associated with non-uniform data formats like E2M1. It highlights the need for alternative approaches, such as the proposed UFP4 recipe, to mitigate these systematic rounding errors and improve pretraining efficiency on various hardware systems.

articles.title: Ensembles of Large Language Models for Identifying EQ-5D Studies in PubMed Based on Their Abstracts
articles.summary: This study explores the application of ensemble methods using large language models, including Google's Gemini, to automate the identification of EQ-5D studies in PubMed based on their abstracts. The approach aims to enhance the efficiency and consistency of systematic literature reviews by reducing the reliance on manual screening.
